This onset carries no word-event formula, koh-amar onset, imperative, or addressee shift of its own — a rhetorical-mode shift rather than any of this book's tier-1 seam classes. Inside the span, no word-event formula and no messenger formula stand at all; imperative forms appear at MT 2:19, 2:23 and 2:25, but as content commands inside the continuing address rather than fresh discourse frames; participant shifts stand at MT 2:28, turning to a masculine-singular vocative naming Judah at וְאַיֵּ֤ה אֱלֹהֶ֨יךָ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂ֣יתָ ... יְהוּדָֽה (oshb:Jer.2.28, byte tier), coinciding with the setumah disclosed inside this span, and at MT 2:29, turning to the plural at כֻּלְּכֶ֛ם פְּשַׁעְתֶּ֥ם בִּ֖י נְאֻם יְהוָֽה (oshb:Jer.2.29, byte tier); neither is adopted as an internal cut here. The indictment moves through the vine (web:Jer.2.21), dromedary and donkey (web:Jer.2.23-24), and idol-futility (web:Jer.2.27-28) metaphors; the unit is held together as one span rather than cut at those metaphor changes, which mark topic, not formula. current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting this span at the vine, dromedary-and-donkey, and idol-futility metaphor changes (web:Jer.2.21, web:Jer.2.23, web:Jer.2.27) was considered and rejected for lacking a formula, imperative, or addressee-shift warrant of the kind that bounds the units on either side of it; those shifts are content transitions inside one sustained divine indictment, held here at medium_low confidence given the length this span reaches without such a warrant appearing inside it. A participant-shift rival was also weighed at MT 2:28 / MT 2:29 — the turn to a masculine-singular vocative naming Judah at וְאַיֵּ֤ה אֱלֹהֶ֨יךָ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂ֣יתָ ... יְהוּדָֽה (oshb:Jer.2.28, byte tier), the first coinciding with the setumah inside this span, and then to the plural at כֻּלְּכֶ֛ם פְּשַׁעְתֶּ֥ם בִּ֖י נְאֻם יְהוָֽה (oshb:Jer.2.29, byte tier), the second closing on its own neum-YHWH formula — but it was not adopted, since no tier-1 onset accompanies either turn to carry a fresh unit by itself.
